newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, lag Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, lag Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities moved into positive territory but lagged Treasuries during a pre-election rally, traders said.

Pass-throughs trailed Treasuries as investors snapped up government paper earlier in the day on hopes President Clinton will win re-election and the Republican party will continue to control the House and the Senate, said one trader.
"The (Treasury) market is betting the results of the election will be status quo," he said, adding that no major changes in policy "will keep the bond market happy for the moment."
Another trader cited a mixed bag of mortgage products that held the market in check.
Sellers of Interest Only (IO) paper and inverse paper sent both a bullish and bearish message to the market, she said.

On the one hand, "the sellers of IO paper were scared to get hurt" by staying in the market, she said. On the other hand, sellers of inverse paper, whose coupon interest rate moves in the opposite direction of interest-rate changes, "were simply taking profits."
By late afternoon Tuesday, pass-throughs were 2/32 to 15/32 higher. Spreads to Treasuries mostly held firm.

Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 13/32 at 100-26/32, yielding 113 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 12/32 at 100-19/32, and Freddie Mac 30-years drifted 14/32 higher to 100-27/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 16/32 to yield 6.28 percent.
